angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 11,415,046 km at 149.25 pc = 1.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: distance 149.254 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.016), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 149.254 +/- 2.388 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 6.5959 +/- 0.2943 mas (same row, RUWE 4.68), 22.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 16.408 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: radius 16.408 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 998.14 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.058) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 11,415,046 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8015 +/- 240 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: effective temperature 8015 +/- 240 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.042) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75097: effective temperature 8015 +/- 240 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.042) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * gam UMi: spectral type A2III (1995ApJS...99..135A)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * gam UMi: main object type dS*, delta Sct Variable
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * gam UMi: projected rotation speed 165 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
